data.name: Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Persian Carpet
data.detailed_description:
Destaque


Acerca do jogo

Proteja-se em seu apartamento londrino na Rua Baker número 221b. O ano é 1896 e a Scotland Yard chamou Sherlock Holmes com um pedido de ajuda urgente. Um jovem pintor foi encontrado assassinado e enrolado em um notável tapete persa. Ao lado de Watson você deve investigar este crime peculiar, explorando as cenas do crime buscando as provas ocultas.
Interaja com os suspeitos, analise os relatórios da polícia e os depoimentos de testemunhas para resolver o crime e desvendar o mistério do tapete persa!
  • Procure nas cenas do crime por objetos ocultos
  • Analise pistas e as descobertas da Polícia
  • Investigue inúmeros suspeitos
  • Revise seu progresso estudando a Mesa de Dedução de Holmes
  • Jogabilidade rica
  • Cenários 3D detalhados e envolventes
  • Música de fundo periódica
  • Pequenos quebra-cabeças adicionais!

data.short_description: Scotland Yard has called Sherlock Holmes with an urgent request for help! A young painter has been found murdered and rolled up in a remarkable Persian carpet. Along with Watson, you must investigate the peculiar crime, exploring crime scene locations in search of missing clues.

reviews.review:
A lazy, asset-flipped cash grab that insults the Sherlock Holmes name.

If you are coming to this game fresh off Frogwares' mainline 3D titles expecting an immersive, atmospheric detective thriller, turn back immediately. This is not a real Sherlock Holmes game; it is a cheaply produced, frustrating 2008 hidden-object spin-off stitched together with old materials.

Here is why you should absolutely avoid it:

• Shameless Asset Flipping: Frogwares didn't bother creating new environments for this game. Instead, they heavily recycled crime scenes and background art straight out of Sherlock Holmes: The Case of the Silver Earring (a game that came out four years prior in 2004).

• The Most Infuriating Pixel Hunts Imaginable: A hidden-object game relies on clever camouflage, but this title crosses the line into complete absurdity. You will spend huge chunks of time furiously clicking around low-resolution, blurry screens trying to find dynamic items that are literally the size of a grain of sand—like a specific stray strand of hair or an invisible smudge of dust that is the exact same colour as the floor.

• Completely Unplayable Hint System: Because the items are impossibly small, you will naturally look to the game's hint system. Shockingly, the developers put a strict, non-replenishing cap of seven hints per level. Once you run out of hints, you are left completely stranded, forcing you to have a third-party internet walkthrough open just to make basic progress.

• Lifeless Presentation: There is zero voice acting in this game. The story is told through dry, silent text boxes slapped onto frozen, un-animated character cutouts. It strips away all narrative tension and makes it impossible to care about the case or the characters.
• Terrible Modern PC Optimization: The game is locked to a rigid legacy 4:3 aspect ratio. Playing it on a modern screen forces massive black bars onto the sides of your display. Worse, the audio compression is deeply outdated, resulting in awful crackling sounds over the music loops on Windows 10 and 11.

Final Verdict:

Do not waste $10 on a shallow 2-hour game that feels like a braindead Frankenstein monstrosity. If you want a casual Sherlock hidden-object experience that actually has passion and high-quality hand-drawn visuals behind it, buy Sherlock Holmes: The Hound of the Baskervilles (2011) instead.
